text:
I propose four WebMCP tools that cover FST's real visitor journeys while keeping WhatsApp sending, privacy consent and Calendar notifications under human control.

- `ask_fst_site` retrieves sourced answers from published FST content.
- `browse_fst_offerings` searches the structured Malta or Rwanda catalogue and starting fees.
- `prepare_fst_service_request` selects valid items and opens the existing reversible order review.
- `prepare_fst_meeting_request` fills the booking form but leaves consent and submission to the visitor.

All four use FST's client-safe content, same-origin APIs or existing UI state. Direct WhatsApp sending and automatic Calendar creation are deliberately excluded. Review each tool, comment or omit any tool, then submit the approved set to begin implementation.

All four approved tools are built and ready for code review. TypeScript, scoped lint, five WebMCP contract tests and `git diff --check` pass. The registration batches explicitly disable SDK telemetry, catalogue preparation stops at the visible WhatsApp review, and booking preparation leaves consent and Calendar submission to the visitor. Review the generated code for each tool in Explorer; approve to start full build, runtime registration and safe local invocation checks, or leave feedback on any tool.

All four approved WebMCP tools are runtime verified and available in pull request https://github.com/ikanisa/FST/pull/1. Full TypeScript, ESLint, production build and 51-test validation pass. WhatsApp sending, privacy consent, booking submission, Calendar creation and invitations remain human-controlled.
